luke.13.p1.b1.text: At that time some of those present told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

luke.13.p1.b2.text: “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this fate?

luke.13.p1.b3.text: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.

luke.13.p2.b1.text: Or those eighteen who were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them:

luke.13.p2.b2.text: Do you think that they were more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem?

luke.13.p2.b3.text: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.”

luke.13.p3.b1.text: “A man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard. He went to look for fruit on it, but did not find any.

luke.13.p3.b2.text: Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?’

luke.13.p3.b3.text: ‘leave it alone again this year, until I dig around it and fertilize it. If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, you can cut it down.’

luke.13.p4.b1.text: One Sabbath Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues,

luke.13.p4.b2.text: and a woman there had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was hunched over and could not stand up straight.

luke.13.p5.b1.text: “Woman, you are set free from your disability.”

luke.13.p5.b2.text: Then He placed His hands on her,

luke.13.p5.b3.text: and immediately she straightened up and began to glorify God.

luke.13.p6.b1.text: “There are six days for work,” … “So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath.”

luke.13.p6.b3.text: “Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it to water?

luke.13.p7.b1.text: Then should not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be released from her bondage on the Sabbath day?”

luke.13.p7.b2.text: When Jesus said this, all His adversaries were humiliated.

luke.13.p7.b3.text: And the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things He was doing.

luke.13.p8.b1.text: “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?

luke.13.p8.b2.text: It is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches.”

luke.13.p8.b3.text: It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.”

luke.13.p9.b1.text: Then Jesus traveled throughout the towns and villages, teaching as He made His way toward Jerusalem.

luke.13.p9.b2.text: “Lord,” … “will only a few people be saved?”

luke.13.p9.b3.text: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door.

luke.13.p10.b1.text: ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’

luke.13.p10.b2.text: ‘I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, …’

luke.13.p10.b3.text: People will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.

luke.13.p10.b4.text: And indeed, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.”

luke.13.p11.b1.text: At that very hour, some Pharisees came to Jesus and told Him,

luke.13.p11.b2.text: “Leave this place and get away, because Herod wants to kill You.”

luke.13.p11.b3.text: “Go tell that fox, ‘Look, I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach My goal.’

luke.13.p11.b4.text: Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, for it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.

luke.13.p12.b1.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her,

luke.13.p12.b2.text: how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!

luke.13.p12.b3.text: Look, your house is left to you desolate. … until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’
